sources: x3d-blender-io@044bea3, x3d.accrete@93063bf, x3d.castle@5b13f70, x3d.chess@17e0d05, x3d.demo@da6513b, x3d.docs@ef0ee74, x3d.gamelab@e0a0d97, x3d.gobbler@9ab6305, x3d.lab@37251e8, x3d.loom@ab462db, x3d.mashtots@3b57769, x3d.mathslab@d883fb7, x3d.ml@ef94650, x3d.music@355af58, x3d.stem@98f79d7, x3d_mcp@fa5dccf

charts.title: Heat terrain
charts.gain: Height repeats the colour channel, so magnitude reads twice: colour for class, height for rank. Orbit low across a row and the 24 x 33 matrix becomes a skyline you can compare by silhouette; look straight down and it is the 2D heatmap again (viewpoint 3).

charts.title: Chord dome (interactive)
charts.gain: Two variables per ribbon instead of one: arch height = files shared (sqrt), tube radius = Jaccard overlap, so a thick low arch is a tight pair of rare types and a thin high arch is two common types that merely co-occur. Click any arch to isolate it (X3D TouchSensor), and the 20 strongest arches carry beads whose speed follows flow. Viewpoint 3 stands you under the dome.

charts.title: Treemap city
charts.gain: A flat treemap shows the hierarchy only as nested borders. Here each level is a terrace (demo, then version), so the nesting is literally visible as terrain, and every file is a tower: area = bytes, height = log bytes, and .x3d files are drawn in a brighter, metallic finish so the scenes stand out from their vendor code.

charts.title: Space-time cube (sliced)
charts.gain: Time is the vertical axis (Hagerstrand space-time cube), so the whole history is on screen at once; now a one-day slab sweeps up and cuts it: everything already happened is lit and solid, everything still to come is a ghost. Two X3D ClipPlanes ride the slab inside counter-moving Transforms, so the cut is done by the renderer, not by script. A repository that dominates a day pulls in toward the axis.

charts.title: 3D force graph
charts.gain: A force layout in 2D must flatten clusters onto each other; with a third degree of freedom the same forces settle with fewer crossings and the components (colour) separate into lobes you can orbit around. Same D3 force model, numDimensions = 3.

charts.title: Sankey canyon (pulses + tour)
charts.gain: In 2D every ribbon shares one plane, so flows from different sources cross and blend. Here each source owns a depth lane and the ribbon is a solid with width = value, so you can look down the canyon and follow one demo through components to node types; the front view (viewpoint 2) is the exact D3 layout. v2 adds light beads that pulse along every ribbon above 1% of the flow (count and size by value, each an X3D PositionInterpolator) and a five-stop fly-through that follows the largest path, from the canyon mouth through the biggest demo, its biggest component and node type, to the exit.

charts.title: 3D scatter
charts.gain: A third real variable (XML nesting depth) instead of a third encoding squeezed into size or colour, and the three 2D scatters D3 would draw are cast as shadows on the floor and two walls, so you get the 3D cloud and all of its projections in one scene.

charts.title: Ridgeline wall
charts.gain: Sixteen lines on one 2D axis overplot into spaghetti. Giving each series its own depth row turns them into a ridgeline you can orbit: the front view still overlays them like the D3 chart, the side view lines up every burst on the same day.

charts.title: Living graph (live, grows through time)
charts.gain: The bridge running live, and in time: press Play and the graph grows demo by demo in the order they shipped (first commit in x3d.demo), each arrival re-heating the 3D forces so its node types pull into place. Demos are metallic crystals, node types are spheres coloured by X3D component, every component is a translucent hull sphere that resizes as its types gather, and edges bend toward their component (bundling) so the structure reads as lobes, not a hairball. Click any node to isolate it with its neighbours. D3 owns the physics; X3D owns light, material, picking and navigation.

charts.title: Sphere packing
charts.gain: Circle packing shows nesting only as circles inside circles; deep levels get tiny and flat. Lifting each level onto its own tier and turning the leaves into spheres lets you read nesting as height and bytes as volume, and low viewpoints show which demo is heavy with images versus scenes at a glance.

charts.title: Violins of revolution
charts.gain: A 2D violin mirrors the density for symmetry only. Spinning it into a solid of revolution makes the mirror meaningful: volume reads as mass, so you see where the work piles up across the day; the gold ring is the median and the silver rings the quartiles.

charts.title: Relief slider
charts.gain: A 2D before/after slider wipes between two pictures. In 3D the second picture is the same image raised into terrain by luminance, so the slider becomes a morph and grazing light reveals structure that colour alone hides.

charts.title: Type sphere
charts.gain: A radial tree spreads its leaves around one circle: 260 X3D node types would be packed at under 1.4 degrees apart. On a sphere the leaves get a whole surface (Fibonacci spiral in D3 cluster order), abstract types sit inside at their depth, and the types his demos actually use glow, so the used part of the spec shows as lit regions.

charts.title: Cone tree
charts.gain: A tidy tree grows only sideways, so a wide level (x3d.loom has many top folders) runs off the page. The cone tree (Xerox PARC, 1991) spends the third dimension on breadth: children ring their parent, so a level of any width fits in one cone and the translucent cones show each family as a unit.

charts.title: Project globe
d3: d3-geo (geoContains, geoArea, geoCentroid, geoInterpolate, geoGraticule10, geoEqualEarth)
charts.gain: Every flat map trades one distortion for another. On a sphere the countries keep true shape and the spikes (height = sqrt of area from d3.geoArea) stand on the real surface; the Equal Earth plate below is the exact 2D projection D3 would draw from the same features, so you can compare the two. v2 adds the project's own world: great-circle arcs (d3.geoInterpolate, lifted in proportion to their length) fly from Blacksburg to Giza, Hawara, Rome, Turin and Yerevan, beads ride them, and each site carries a beacon whose height is log2 of the commits behind that site's work.

charts.title: Particle type
charts.gain: Flat particle text has only x and y to scatter into. Here the letters have real thickness (sigma 0.22 in z), the scatter is a 3D cloud, and a swirl phase rotates the word through depth, so orbiting mid-animation shows parallax that a 2D canvas cannot.
